name: Tengri
role: Sky god and the highest power of the eternal blue sky
fun_fact: The Secret History calls him Mongke Tngri, Eternal Heaven, and Turkic khans styled themselves 'Tengri-born'.

name: Umay
role: Goddess of children, the womb and the hearth
fun_fact: An eighth-century Turkic inscription praises a queen as 'like the goddess Umay', which makes her one of the earliest attested steppe deities.

name: Geser
role: Heavenly hero who clears the world of demons
fun_fact: The first printed Geser was a Mongolian woodblock made in Beijing in 1716, while Buryat singers know him as Abai Geser Khubun.

name: Manas
role: Kyrgyz hero who unites the tribes
fun_fact: One manaschi, Doolot Sydykov, recited the epic for 111 hours over five days in 2021.

name: Erlik
role: Ruler of the dead and the underworld
fun_fact: Mongol speakers call him Erleg, and the Orkhon inscriptions already mention a lord of the underworld.

name: Shaman
role: Ritual specialist who journeys between the worlds
fun_fact: Mongol male shamans are called böö and female shamans udgan, and Buryat practice often lives alongside Buddhism.

name: Swan Maiden
role: Heavenly woman who becomes an ancestress
fun_fact: The Khori Buryats honour swans as kin, will not kill them, and sprinkle milk after passing flocks.

name: Bayan Khongor
role: Hunter who marries the swan maiden
fun_fact: Recorded Buryat tellings usually call the hunter Khoridoy Mergen, and Bayan Khongor is also the name of a mountain in Buryatia.

name: Kanikey
role: Wife of Manas and the epic's wisest adviser
fun_fact: Legend says she had a misleading inscription carved on Manas's tomb at Talas so that his enemies would not find him.

name: Almambet
role: Prince from China who becomes Manas's sworn brother
fun_fact: Almambet is remembered as an outsider who chose Manas, and his loyalty is one of the epic's most quoted examples of friendship.
